tasks.short: Develop and test sports emergency procedures

steps.what: Inspect venue access, equipment and emergency response constraints
Agree emergency roles and response arrangements with venue staff
Develop emergency procedures for practices and competitions using verified venue arrangements
Rehearse emergency scenarios and test venue response arrangements
Correct and check emergency instructions against drill findings

tasks.design: Configure the existing {DOCS} procedure template with reusable role tables, venue fields and section layout. The physician enters the actual venue findings and agreed arrangements, tests them with people and corrects the final instructions; ordinary author saves remain part of writing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Venue procedures mix reusable headings with local access routes, equipment and people.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document templates can remove repeated layout and field placement without generating emergency decisions.
tasks.still_hard: A written route or response role can look plausible while failing in a real venue.
tasks.human_edge: The physician spots unsafe arrangements during drills and negotiates workable responsibilities.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less document assembly; emergency response authority stays the same.

reach.task: Rehearse emergency response at training venues
reach.learn: Venue access checks and multidisciplinary drill observation

evidence.claim: Configurable document templates can reuse fields and layout; this is model knowledge, not a measured sports emergency case.

assumptions: Boundary is procedure development and physical testing, not dispatch during a real emergency or an unobserved distribution process.
The physician produces venue access, equipment location, response role and contact fields through s1 and s2. No clean venue feed is assumed; unique instructions are typed and checked within s3.
Test native document templates first. Of s3's 20 hours, five are repeated table and heading assembly; fifteen remain for first capture and instruction wording. All ten correction hours in s5 remain.
The shared procedure is the actual document used by the venue response team. No separate drill log or routine record is added. Internal author saves have no gate and no saving.
unknowns: Whether procedures already use equivalent templates
Which venues require wholly different response arrangements
research_questions: Can current templates reuse the role table without hiding venue-specific constraints?

already_counted.description: Enter and check venue-specific instructions, then correct them after drills

incremental.description: Maintain procedure template fields and test layout after changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: five hours of repeated layout removed, less 0.5 template upkeep, gives 4.5. Cautious case: an unusual venue needs a bespoke document or already has the reusable layout; all twenty writing hours remain and the extra template is not maintained. Drills, consultation and correction remain in both cases.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read current treatment plans and outstanding care questions in clinical records
Discuss care conflicts, progress and responsibilities with other experts
Record agreed care actions, owners and follow-up dates
Check final handover content and permitted clinical recipients
Send the checked care handover to the selected clinical recipients

tasks.design: Configure a current-plan view in the {OTHER} clinical-record system and its existing secure handover facility. The physician still reads the substance, talks with experts and first records the agreed actions; the final content and recipients are checked before the actual send.
tasks.previous_blocker: Current plans and action ownership can require several record views, followed by a separate handover send.
tasks.enabler_now: Native clinical views and recipient-bound notifications can reduce navigation and dispatch handling.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting care advice and what information each recipient may receive require clinical judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The physician reconciles specialties and ensures the team understands responsibilities.
tasks.altitude: Less navigation and send handling; care coordination and clinical decisions remain with the physician.

reach.task: Agree rehabilitation responsibilities with the treating team
reach.learn: Rehabilitation milestones and concise clinical handover

evidence.claim: Native record views and configured notifications can reduce navigation and sending; this is model knowledge, not a measured care-coordination saving.

assumptions: Boundary covers a coordination discussion with an actual subsequent handover, including first entry of the agreement. There is no automatic clinical recommendation.

Treating professionals already produce patient identifier, dated plan version, author, current action and owner in clinical records. The physician manually obtains missing or conflicting information within s1 and s2; their existing record work is not claimed as a saving.

Test native current-plan views first. Only two of twenty context-reading hours are navigation; eighteen hours of interpretation remain. The one-hour send is actual recipient dispatch, not the ordinary internal save inside s3.
The clinical record and handover system must support exact version and recipient binding. A changed plan or recipient list invalidates approval.
unknowns: Whether experts share the same clinical record
Which recipients need separate secure exchange
Whether a current-plan view already exists
research_questions: Can the native handover send use the exact checked entry and permitted recipients?

already_counted.description: Interpret current plans, first capture agreements and check final handover meaning and recipients

incremental.description: Check record-view fields and notification failures after changes

approvals.approved_version: Exact care coordination entry, handover payload and recipient list checked in s4; edits require a new check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: two hours of navigation plus one actual dispatch hour removed, less 0.5 upkeep, gives 2.5. Cautious case: external specialists' incompatible records retain all twenty context hours; the supported secure send still removes one hour, less 0.5 upkeep. First capture, consultation and meaning checks remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe and evaluate athletes' mental well-being

steps.what: Observe athletes' behaviour and changes during sporting activity
Discuss mood, concerns and functioning privately with the athlete
Evaluate mental well-being and decide whether further assessment is needed
Enter and verify relevant well-being findings in clinical records
Save the author's verified clinical entry

tasks.design: Keep observation, confidential conversation and mental well-being evaluation with the physician. In the {OTHER} clinical-record system, test a native encounter template that supplies existing patient and encounter headers while the physician first enters and verifies the actual findings.
tasks.previous_blocker: The substantive assessment depends on trust and context; a small amount of entry repeats encounter context.
tasks.enabler_now: Native encounter templates can supply already selected patient and date fields.
tasks.still_hard: Distress can be hidden, contextual or expressed indirectly.
tasks.human_edge: The physician earns trust and interprets changes without treating a generated score as an assessment.
tasks.altitude: The week and decision rights barely change; only repeated header entry may shrink.

reach.task: Recognise when a patient needs specialist mental-health assessment
reach.learn: Referral thresholds and sensitive clinical communication

evidence.claim: Encounter templates can supply existing identifiers and dates; this is model knowledge and does not support automated mental well-being evaluation.

assumptions: Boundary is observation and clinical evaluation plus the associated clinical entry, not a later referral or message to a coach.

The clinical-record system already holds the selected patient identifier and encounter date. The physician produces all new observations and assessment text in s4; absent header fields are entered manually within the retained time.

Native configuration is tested first. Only 0.45 of nine entry hours represents repeated headers; 8.55 hours of first capture and clinical verification remain. The one-hour ordinary author save stays fully retained without approval.
No ambient recording, automatic risk classification, routine athlete surveillance log or automatic sharing is introduced.
unknowns: Whether encounter headers are already supplied
How frequently substantive findings require clinical entry
research_questions: Is there any repeated header entry left after using the native encounter screen?

already_counted.description: First capture and clinical verification of the actual well-being findings

incremental.description: Check encounter header defaults after record-system changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: 0.45 header-entry hours removed less 0.1 upkeep gives 0.35, rounded down to 0.3. Cautious case: the current encounter screen already supplies patient and date; all ten record hours remain and no additional configuration or upkeep is introduced. Observation, conversation and evaluation retain all ninety hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Advise changes to potentially harmful sports practices

steps.what: Review the athlete's activity, symptoms and relevant clinical findings
Decide which sports practices should change or stop
Explain activity changes and address athlete or coach concerns
Write the actual activity restrictions and reassessment conditions
Check final written restrictions and the intended recipient
Hand the checked written activity instructions to the intended recipient

tasks.design: Use a native {DOCS} activity-instruction template for headings and existing identity fields. The physician chooses the restrictions, explains them, first writes the individual conditions and checks the exact final handout before handing it to the athlete or authorised coach.
tasks.previous_blocker: Individual activity limits cannot be inferred safely from generic sports advice; only document layout repeats.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing templates can remove repeated header and layout work while keeping the actual advice handwritten or typed by the physician.
tasks.still_hard: Advice may threaten an athlete's selection or career and needs careful explanation.
tasks.human_edge: The physician weighs harm, uncertainty and the athlete's goals, then secures understanding.
tasks.altitude: A little less handout preparation; authority over sports restrictions is unchanged.

reach.task: Adapt training around physician-imposed activity restrictions
reach.learn: Clear functional restrictions and reassessment conditions

evidence.claim: Native document templates can reuse headings and identity fields; this is model knowledge, not evidence for automatically choosing activity restrictions.

assumptions: This branch includes an actual written instruction that the athlete uses between visits. Purely verbal advice has no invented handout, follow-up log or automatic send.

The physician produces activity, restriction, duration and reassessment conditions in s4 from the clinical decision. Existing patient identity is checked manually; missing fields are typed within the nine retained writing hours.
Test native templates first. One of ten writing hours is repeated heading and layout work; all advice wording, ordinary author saves, final verification and physical delivery remain.
Approval binds the final handout and intended recipient after writing; it gates the physical disclosure, not an internal author save. Changes require a fresh check.
unknowns: Whether written instructions already use a template
Whether any coach may receive the individual instructions
research_questions: Do existing handout templates already remove all repeated layout work?

already_counted.description: First write the individual restrictions and verify the final meaning and recipient

incremental.description: Maintain the instruction layout without introducing default clinical restrictions

approvals.approved_version: Exact activity-instruction handout and intended recipient checked in s5; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: one repeated layout hour removed, less 0.2 upkeep, gives 0.8. Cautious case: the advice is entirely verbal or current handouts already have the needed layout, so no template work is removed and no new template upkeep is incurred. Clinical reasoning, explanation and actual delivery remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Small reductions in procedure layout, record navigation and actual handover handling. Clinical reasoning, sensitive conversations and emergency drills still dominate.
reach: Athletic trainer: connect emergency drills and training restrictions to venue realities
Physical therapist: improve multidisciplinary rehabilitation handovers
skills_to_grow: Native clinical-record views and exact recipient checks
Concise activity restrictions and reassessment conditions
role.ambitious_version: A physician whose emergency plans and shared care instructions are clearer, while clinical decisions and athlete trust remain personal responsibilities.
